project genuinely cannot provide (a special Apple entitlement, a paid
developer account feature, server-side ML), do NOT fake or stub it —
record it as an explicit gap with what it would actually take.

Core features (complete over broad — ship fewer things fully working):

1. Voice entries: record audio journal entries with a live waveform
   view while recording. Recording must survive being interrupted by a
   phone call, Siri, or the app being backgrounded, and must resume
   or cleanly finalize the entry rather than corrupt/lose it — get
   AVAudioSession category/interruption handling genuinely right, this
   is the hardest technical part of the app.
2. On-device transcription: transcribe each recording using Speech
   framework (on-device recognition only — reject/flag if only
   server-based recognition is available for a locale). Transcript is
   editable after the fact; edits must not desync from the audio
   timeline (tapping a transcript sentence seeks the audio to that
   point).
3. Auto-tagging & mood: run NaturalLanguage tokenization/sentiment on
   each transcript to suggest tags and a mood score. Suggestions are
   editable/dismissible — never silently apply an AI guess as fact.
4. Sketch annotations: attach PencilKit sketches to any entry (finger
   or Pencil), stored alongside the audio/transcript.
5. Bi-directional linking: entries can @-mention/link other entries;
   each entry shows a "linked from" backlinks section computed live
   from the local store (no manual backlink maintenance) — same
   integrity discipline as a graph/notes app: linking, unlinking, and
   deleting an entry must never leave a dangling or duplicate backlink.
6. Search: full-text search across transcripts AND tags/mood, with
   results ranked by a real relevance score you define and document
   (not just substring match order).
7. HealthKit correlation (read-only, explicit permission): show each
   entry's mood alongside that day's HealthKit sleep/activity summary
   if authorized, and degrade to "not connected" honestly if denied —
   never block core journaling on this permission.
8. Home-screen widget + Live Activity: widget shows the latest entry's
   mood/snippet; a Live Activity shows elapsed time and live waveform

9. Share Extension (separate target): accept shared text or a photo

10. App Intents: "Start a voice entry" and "Search my journal" exposed

    entitlement, which a personal free developer account cannot
    obtain — if that's confirmed true in this environment, build the
    CarPlay scene code path correctly but record in Gaps that it
    cannot actually run/ship without that entitlement, rather than
    silently omitting the feature or pretending it works.

Priorities, in order: (a) audio-session interruption correctness — a
lost or corrupted recording is the worst possible failure, (b) backlink
graph integrity, (c) honest degradation of every permission-gated
feature (Speech, HealthKit, CarPlay). Use Decimal/Int for anything
numeric that isn't inherently floating (durations in seconds as
TimeInterval is fine; don't invent unnecessary Decimal use here — this
app's money-precision lesson from prior apps doesn't apply, there's no
currency). Seed a "demo entries" toggle in Settings with realistic
sample entries, transcripts, tags, and backlinks so no screen is empty
on first review. Provide a clear way to run it in the iOS Simulator via
Xcode, and call out anywhere CarPlay/HealthKit/Speech behave differently

I agree with most of what Claude and Codex already closed, but I want to push one correction: the contract still risks becoming “feature-complete theatre” unless we force a trust-first artifact layer on every phase. Codex set the right priority order; Claude made the right call that interruption claims are mostly theater unless scenario-testable. To make this genuinely remarkable instead of merely ambitious, every phase should deliver an auditable “feature health card” with three visible states: what is guaranteed, what degrades, and what is truly gapped. That keeps the team from calling something “done” because it compiles.

Hard requirements are: full offline-first runtime with zero core-network dependence; all primary behavior implemented in SwiftUI/SwiftData plus AVFoundation/Speech/NaturalLanguage/PencilKit; on-device-only Speech by policy and by runtime state so there is no silent backend fallback; every AI-derived tag/mood suggestion must remain user-controlled; recording and playback must be lifecycle-safe around interruptions and background transitions; backlinks must be computed live from current store state, never cached as separate mutable reverse-edge tables; search must use a documented relevance formula and expose repeatable ranking; HealthKit and Live Activity/Widget/Share Extension/App Intents are read/write/shared via App Group + shared SwiftData container semantics where required; CarPlay path exists in code but is gapped if entitlement absent; demo entries only appear via explicit toggle and remain clearly labeled non-real.

Non-goals should be explicit and hard-fenced: no cloud sync, no analytics beacons, no account system, no server inference for tagging/mood/transcription, no silent placeholder pretending to be real data, and no pretending entitlement-locked features run without entitlement.

For output shape in later phases, I want this to be strict: each phase should produce an updated contract section and a test evidence slice (device + simulator matrix), plus a gap register entry with blocker, exact Apple/API cause, and unblock recipe. The phase is ready for handoff only when each numbered requirement has both status and evidence, not just code touched.

Production-ready here should mean zero-corruption trust under stress and deterministic degradations. I’d define it as: “the app behaves correctly on device in the face of interruptions, permission loss, and lifecycle transitions, and whenever behavior cannot be provided in this environment, the app surfaces a transparent, actionable gap and never fabricates behavior.” If recording integrity or backlink integrity is weak, the product is not production-ready regardless of feature breadth; I want that line carried as a hard gate, not a philosophical note.

Decision rules for later phases: resolve conflicts by offline-first and data-integrity first, then UX polish; if uncertain about a capability from simulator-only observations, mark it explicitly as device-only unknown and require next-device verification; if a claim says “handles,” it must name concrete API events and observed outcome; if a search ranking claim says “relevant,” the exact formula must be in code comments/docs and tested against a fixed fixture; if an interruption path is tested only once in simulator, it only validates a subset and can never clear the final interruption requirement; if links are edited/deleted, a forward mention to a deleted entry must remain visibly broken rather than silently disappearing, while backlinks section must remain computed-locally and never duplicated.

My sharp disagreement with no one, but a hard improvement: we should standardize mention identity around immutable IDs, not display titles, otherwise backlinks and de-dup fail when titles change and users can create ambiguous duplicates; this strengthens the “no dangling/duplicate” promise and keeps the graph credible. Also, we should include an explicit “Audio Spine Invariants” rule: every sentence-to-time anchor in transcripts is immutable once recorded, edits can be attached as overlay deltas, and seek uses anchor IDs not raw string indexes, which is the only way Claude’s worry about edit desync survives real use.

Okay, reading the coordinator's decision block and Codex's contract — I actually think this landed in a good place, but I want to push on a few spots before we let this contract go final, because a couple of the "resolved" items still have soft edges that a later phase could exploit to claim victory without earning it.

First, on DEC-004, the staleDate-plus-reconciliation answer for Live Activity — I stand by that being the right mechanism, but I want to flag the honesty gap in it explicitly rather than let it read as fully solved. If a user force-quits mid-recording and doesn't reopen the app for two days, the Live Activity sits there until either the system's own staleness dimming kicks in or the user relaunches and the app's reconciliation code runs. That's a real window where "no orphaned Live Activity" isn't strictly true — it's "no orphaned Live Activity once you give the app a chance to clean up, backstopped by iOS's own staleness UI." That's a fine, honest answer, but the contract should say that explicitly rather than let a later phase report "orphaned Live Activity: solved" as if there's zero window. I'd rather we write the caveat into the decision now than have someone discover it during build verification and treat it as a new bug.

Second — and this is a factual correction to something Codex's testable requirement #27 and my own gap-framing risk conflating — HealthKit reads actually do work fine in the Simulator. You can manually enter sample sleep/activity data into the Simulator's Health app and the HealthKit read APIs behave normally against it; it's not like CarPlay where the entitlement itself is the blocker. The thing that's genuinely gated behind account tier is *distribution* (TestFlight/App Store), not local development or Simulator testing. Coordinator's DEC-006 already gets this basically right by splitting it into two tiers, but I want to make sure the run guide (testable requirement 27) doesn't lump HealthKit in with CarPlay as "device-only, can't verify here" — that would be under-claiming a gap that doesn't exist and would waste effort avoiding a test that's actually possible right now.

Third, on backlinks — I like where DEC-008 landed (compute live, never store, broken-link indicator for a mention pointing at a deleted entry), but there's a requirement hiding inside it that isn't spelled out yet: mentions have to resolve by stable entry ID/UUID, not by matching entry title text. If linking is done by title-string matching, then renaming an entry silently breaks every existing mention of it (they'd all start rendering as broken-link even though the entry still exists), or worse, a rename could cause a mention to silently re-resolve to a different entry that now happens to share that title. That's exactly the kind of "quietly breaks" bug that wouldn't show up in a quick demo-entries walkthrough but would absolutely bite a real user renaming an old entry six months in. I want this nailed down now: @-mentions store a reference to the entry's persistent identifier, full stop, and renaming an entry must not affect any existing link.

Fourth, I want to push back a little on Codex's "20+ manual runs" success metric for interruption correctness. I like that there's a number attached instead of a vague "handles interruptions," but a number alone can be gamed — you can burn through 20 runs of "background the app, come back" and call the metric satisfied while never once testing a phone call arriving mid-recording, or force-quitting via the app switcher during active recording, or recording until the device is nearly out of storage. If we leave "20+ manual runs" unqualified, a later phase will naturally gravitate toward the easiest 20 reps to close out the checklist fastest. I think the fix is cheap: name the scenario mix inside that metric — real incoming call, Siri invocation, backgrounding, force-quit via app switcher during active recording, and (if feasible) a low-storage condition — and require at least one clean pass of each named scenario, not just 20 undifferentiated reps.

Last thing, smaller but worth locking in before we move on: search needs an explicit answer for entries that have no transcript yet (because Speech was unavailable for that locale, or transcription is still running). Testable requirement 14 says search covers transcript + tags + mood — fine — but I want the contract to say plainly that an untranscribed entry is still findable via its tags/mood/sketch metadata, and that this is expected behavior, not a bug where "search seems to be missing an entry." Otherwise whoever does the build-verification pass on search is going to stumble on that and not know if it's a defect or a documented limitation.

None of this contradicts Codex's contract or the coordinator's decisions — I'm not proposing a different plan, I'm tightening four soft spots (Live Activity's honest residual window, the HealthKit-Simulator factual correction, ID-based mention resolution instead of title matching, and a scenario-named interruption metric instead of an undifferentiated rep count) plus one documentation gap (search behavior for untranscribed entries) so that later phases can't satisfy the letter of a requirement while missing what it was actually protecting against.

Round two didn't surface any real disagreement — Codex and Claude (independently) converged on the same fix for mention identity (resolve by immutable ID, not title text), and everything else was each side tightening soft edges in what was already agreed rather than proposing a different plan. This is genuine convergence, not forced agreement — nobody's contract got overridden, four gaps just got closed with concrete, testable language.

What changed this round: Codex added two structural pieces — an "Audio Spine Invariants" rule (transcript sentence-to-time anchors are immutable once recorded, edits are overlay deltas, seeking always resolves by anchor ID never raw string offset, which is literally what makes tap-to-seek survive editing) and a requirement that every phase produce a "feature health card" per requirement (guaranteed / degrades / gapped, with evidence) instead of a bare "done." ## Final Output

The contract from round 1 stands, with these additions locked in:

- **Mention identity:** @-mentions and backlinks resolve by the entry's persistent UUID, never by matching title text. Renaming an entry must never break or misdirect an existing mention — this is what keeps the "no dangling/duplicate backlink" promise credible under real use (people rename things).
- **Audio Spine Invariants:** transcript sentence-to-audio-timestamp anchors are immutable once created; user edits to transcript text layer on as overlay deltas; seeking always resolves via anchor ID, never a raw string/character index. This is the actual mechanism that keeps tap-to-seek accurate after a transcript edit.
- **Live Activity honesty caveat:** "no orphaned Live Activity" means no orphan once the app gets a chance to reconcile (staleDate + reconciliation on next launch), backstopped by iOS's own staleness dimming — there's a real window between a force-quit and the next relaunch where the activity is still visually present. State this caveat explicitly wherever this requirement is claimed as done; don't imply a zero-window guarantee.
- **HealthKit — factual correction:** HealthKit reads work normally in the Simulator against manually-entered sample Health data. The only actual gate is TestFlight/App Store *distribution* needing a paid developer account — not local development or Simulator testing. The run guide must not group HealthKit with CarPlay as "can't verify here."
- **Interruption metric, named not just counted:** the 20+ manual test runs must include at least one clean verified pass of each of: a real incoming phone call, a Siri invocation, app backgrounding, a force-quit via app switcher during active recording, and (if feasible) a low-storage condition — not just 20 undifferentiated reps of the easiest scenario.
- **Search documentation:** an entry with no transcript yet (Speech unavailable for its locale, or still processing) is still findable via its tags, mood, and sketch metadata. This is documented expected behavior, so it isn't mistaken for a defect during verification.
- **Feature health cards:** every later phase reports each numbered requirement's status as guaranteed / degrades / gapped, with supporting evidence — not a bare "done." A phase isn't handoff-ready until every requirement has both.

I agree with most of what Claude and Codex already closed, but I want to push one correction: the contract still risks becoming “feature-complete theatre” unless we force a trust-first artifact layer on every phase. Codex set the right priority order; Claude made the right call that interruption claims are mostly theater unless scenario-testable. To make this genuinely remarkable instead of merely ambitious, every phase should deliver an auditable “feature health card” with three visible states: what is guaranteed, what degrades, and what is truly gapped. That keeps the team from calling something “done” because it compiles.

Hard requirements are: full offline-first runtime with zero core-network dependence; all primary behavior implemented in SwiftUI/SwiftData plus AVFoundation/Speech/NaturalLanguage/PencilKit; on-device-only Speech by policy and by runtime state so there is no silent backend fallback; every AI-derived tag/mood suggestion must remain user-controlled; recording and playback must be lifecycle-safe around interruptions and background transitions; backlinks must be computed live from current store state, never cached as separate mutable reverse-edge tables; search must use a documented relevance formula and expose repeatable ranking; HealthKit and Live Activity/Widget/Share Extension/App Intents are read/write/shared via App Group + shared SwiftData container semantics where required; CarPlay path exists in code but is gapped if entitlement absent; demo entries only appear via explicit toggle and remain clearly labeled non-real.

Non-goals should be explicit and hard-fenced: no cloud sync, no analytics beacons, no account system, no server inference for tagging/mood/transcription, no silent placeholder pretending to be real data, and no pretending entitlement-locked features run without entitlement.

For output shape in later phases, I want this to be strict: each phase should produce an updated contract section and a test evidence slice (device + simulator matrix), plus a gap register entry with blocker, exact Apple/API cause, and unblock recipe. The phase is ready for handoff only when each numbered requirement has both status and evidence, not just code touched.

Production-ready here should mean zero-corruption trust under stress and deterministic degradations. I’d define it as: “the app behaves correctly on device in the face of interruptions, permission loss, and lifecycle transitions, and whenever behavior cannot be provided in this environment, the app surfaces a transparent, actionable gap and never fabricates behavior.” If recording integrity or backlink integrity is weak, the product is not production-ready regardless of feature breadth; I want that line carried as a hard gate, not a philosophical note.

Decision rules for later phases: resolve conflicts by offline-first and data-integrity first, then UX polish; if uncertain about a capability from simulator-only observations, mark it explicitly as device-only unknown and require next-device verification; if a claim says “handles,” it must name concrete API events and observed outcome; if a search ranking claim says “relevant,” the exact formula must be in code comments/docs and tested against a fixed fixture; if an interruption path is tested only once in simulator, it only validates a subset and can never clear the final interruption requirement; if links are edited/deleted, a forward mention to a deleted entry must remain visibly broken rather than silently disappearing, while backlinks section must remain computed-locally and never duplicated.

First, on DEC-004, the staleDate-plus-reconciliation answer for Live Activity — I stand by that being the right mechanism, but I want to flag the honesty gap in it explicitly rather than let it read as fully solved. If a user force-quits mid-recording and doesn't reopen the app for two days, the Live Activity sits there until either the system's own staleness dimming kicks in or the user relaunches and the app's reconciliation code runs. That's a real window where "no orphaned Live Activity" isn't strictly true — it's "no orphaned Live Activity once you give the app a chance to clean up, backstopped by iOS's own staleness UI." That's a fine, honest answer, but the contract should say that explicitly rather than let a later phase report "orphaned Live Activity: solved" as if there's zero window. I'd rather we write the caveat into the decision now than have someone discover it during build verification and treat it as a new bug.

Second — and this is a factual correction to something Codex's testable requirement #27 and my own gap-framing risk conflating — HealthKit reads actually do work fine in the Simulator. You can manually enter sample sleep/activity data into the Simulator's Health app and the HealthKit read APIs behave normally against it; it's not like CarPlay where the entitlement itself is the blocker. The thing that's genuinely gated behind account tier is *distribution* (TestFlight/App Store), not local development or Simulator testing. Coordinator's DEC-006 already gets this basically right by splitting it into two tiers, but I want to make sure the run guide (testable requirement 27) doesn't lump HealthKit in with CarPlay as "device-only, can't verify here" — that would be under-claiming a gap that doesn't exist and would waste effort avoiding a test that's actually possible right now.

Third, on backlinks — I like where DEC-008 landed (compute live, never store, broken-link indicator for a mention pointing at a deleted entry), but there's a requirement hiding inside it that isn't spelled out yet: mentions have to resolve by stable entry ID/UUID, not by matching entry title text. If linking is done by title-string matching, then renaming an entry silently breaks every existing mention of it (they'd all start rendering as broken-link even though the entry still exists), or worse, a rename could cause a mention to silently re-resolve to a different entry that now happens to share that title. That's exactly the kind of "quietly breaks" bug that wouldn't show up in a quick demo-entries walkthrough but would absolutely bite a real user renaming an old entry six months in. I want this nailed down now: @-mentions store a reference to the entry's persistent identifier, full stop, and renaming an entry must not affect any existing link.

Fourth, I want to push back a little on Codex's "20+ manual runs" success metric for interruption correctness. I like that there's a number attached instead of a vague "handles interruptions," but a number alone can be gamed — you can burn through 20 runs of "background the app, come back" and call the metric satisfied while never once testing a phone call arriving mid-recording, or force-quitting via the app switcher during active recording, or recording until the device is nearly out of storage. If we leave "20+ manual runs" unqualified, a later phase will naturally gravitate toward the easiest 20 reps to close out the checklist fastest. # First-Party Apple Frameworks Cheatsheet (iOS 17+ / Swift 5.9+)

Build capable iPhone apps with **zero third-party dependencies**. For each framework: when to reach for it, the entry-point type, and a compilable, idiomatic snippet or the gotcha that bites people. All examples target **iOS 17 minimum** unless a call-out says otherwise; Swift Concurrency (`async`/`await`) is preferred over completion handlers everywhere Apple offers it.

## General rules

- **Prefer these over SPM packages.** RevenueCat, Firebase Analytics, Lottie, Alamofire, etc. all have first-party equivalents good enough for most apps. Fewer deps = smaller binary, faster builds, no supply-chain risk, no privacy-manifest surprises.
- **Every framework that touches user data needs an `Info.plist` usage-description string** (or an entitlement). Missing it is a runtime crash the moment the API is used — not a compile error. The specific keys are listed per section.
- **Import the framework and its SwiftUI companion when one exists** (e.g. `import MapKit` gives you `Map`; `import StoreKit` gives you `SubscriptionStoreView`/`StoreView`).
- **Do capability checks before hardware-dependent APIs** (`CHHapticEngine.capabilitiesForHardware().supportsHaptics`, `HKHealthStore.isHealthDataAvailable()`, `GKLocalPlayer.local.isAuthenticated`). Simulators and older/cheaper devices lie.
- **Never block the main actor.** Long queries, audio-graph setup, and StoreKit calls belong in `Task {}` or `async` functions.
- **Verify APIs against the deployment target.** Several SwiftUI conveniences (e.g. `GameCenterView`, Control widgets) shipped *after* iOS 17. Availability call-outs below flag these.

## StoreKit 2 — In-App Purchase & Subscriptions

**Use it when:** you sell anything — consumables, non-consumables, or auto-renewable subscriptions. Replaces callback-based StoreKit 1 entirely.

**Start from:** `Product` (fetch + purchase) and `Transaction` (entitlements + history). No server strictly required — signatures are verified on-device via `VerificationResult`.

### The three things you must do

1. **Load products by ID** (IDs come from App Store Connect):

```swift
import StoreKit

let productIDs = ["com.app.pro.monthly", "com.app.pro.yearly", "com.app.coins.100"]
let products = try await Product.products(for: productIDs)   // async throws
```

2. **Purchase, then verify and finish the transaction:**

```swift
func purchase(_ product: Product) async throws -> Transaction? {
    let result = try await product.purchase()
    switch result {
    case .success(let verification):
        let transaction = try checkVerified(verification)
        await transaction.finish()          // REQUIRED — unfinished txns replay forever
        return transaction
    case .userCancelled, .pending:
        return nil
    @unknown default:
        return nil
    }
}

func checkVerified<T>(_ result: VerificationResult<T>) throws -> T {
    switch result {
    case .unverified(_, let error): throw error   // signature failed — do NOT grant
    case .verified(let safe):       return safe
    }
}
```

3. **Listen for `Transaction.updates` from app launch** — the single most-missed requirement. It catches renewals, Ask-to-Buy approvals, refunds, and purchases made on other devices.

```swift
// Start this in your App init / a top-level task and keep it alive for the app's lifetime.
func observeTransactions() -> Task<Void, Never> {
    Task.detached {
        for await update in Transaction.updates {
            guard case .verified(let transaction) = update else { continue }
            await grantEntitlement(for: transaction)   // your unlock logic
            await transaction.finish()
        }
    }
}
```

Use `Transaction.currentEntitlements` (an async sequence). **iOS 18.4+ note:** the per-product `Transaction.currentEntitlement(for:)` is deprecated in favor of `Transaction.currentEntitlements(for:)`, because a user can hold multiple entitling transactions (e.g. own it *and* have Family Sharing access).

```swift
func hasActiveSubscription() async -> Bool {
    for await result in Transaction.currentEntitlements {
        guard case .verified(let transaction) = result else { continue }
        if transaction.productType == .autoRenewable && transaction.revocationDate == nil {

    }
    return false
